items.title: SME S109 — Replace request polling with a streaming duplex session
items.scope: Live-path transport only; ledger, storage and Atlas boundaries unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Browser and service exchange audio and turn events over one authenticated local streaming session; no polling loop remains on the live path.
Every event carries session, turn, transcript revision and generation identifiers so a late result can neither speak nor mutate the current turn.
Disconnect and restart resume the session with an explicit audio-gap notice.
Push-to-talk continues to work when streaming is unavailable, as a fallback rather than the default path.

items.title: SME S110 — Listen continuously with voice-activity detection and streaming recognition
items.scope: Capture, voice-activity detection, endpointing and recogniser selection; extends the recognition evidence in #1520.
acceptance_criteria: The microphone stays open for the agreed session with a visible state and a working mute; partial transcripts stabilise while the participant speaks.
A persistent streaming recogniser replaces per-utterance process spawning; base.en is compared with at least one larger local model on numbers, negation, acronyms, hesitation and noise.
Premature turn-cut rate at or below 5 per cent on labelled turn cases, reported with numerator and denominator; hesitation and silence are distinguished from a completed thought.
Provisional text remains provisional: only stabilised or confirmed wording can support a claim.

items.title: SME S111 — Stop speaking when the participant speaks
items.scope: Acoustic barge-in and echo handling on the confirmed headset.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed participant speech onset to cessation of played output at or below 250 ms p95 on labelled cases.
Echo cancellation prevents the interviewer's own output being treated as participant speech; evidence covers headset playback.
Queued and in-flight synthesis and generation are cancelled; no stale response speaks after an interruption.
A participant pause, mute or button press always takes precedence over any model plan.

items.title: SME S112 — Split the fast talker from the background thinker
items.scope: Question planning and response composition; check placement follows ADR-013 and ADR-014.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage assessment, claim drafting, evidence matching and agenda maintenance run from partial transcripts while the participant is still speaking.
The spoken reply is produced by a fast non-reasoning local model from the prepared agenda; no model review call remains on the critical path.
End of speech to first substantive audio at p50 at or below 1.5 s and p95 at or below 3 s over at least 100 in-browser turns, instrumented per SME-S114.
Pre-rendered filler that only masks delay is removed; any acknowledgement is contextual and is reported separately from the substantive response.
Ledger, draft and publication checks are unchanged and keep their full model review off the speech path.

items.title: SME S113 — Speak in streamed clauses with an acknowledgement bank
items.scope: Synthesis boundary and playback only; voice selection stays with SME-S118.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesis emits first audio within 400 ms of the first checked clause instead of waiting for a complete file.
Cancellation works at clause granularity and leaves no orphaned audio.
Short acknowledgements are pre-rendered and served without a model request; they never carry facts, numbers or names.
Synthesis may alter prosody, never content; number, date and negation rendering regressions remain green.

items.title: SME S114 — Instrument the real turn gap in the browser
items.scope: Measurement and reporting only.
acceptance_criteria: Each turn records endpoint decision, final transcript, first generated token, first audio and playback start with browser-side timestamps.
Per-session latency distributions are exportable and are reported with every conversational iteration, cold start separately from warm.
Reported figures state their sample size; stage figures are never summed into an end-to-end claim.

items.title: SME S115 — Let the interviewer speak like an interviewer
items.scope: Response grammar, persona and speech-safety checks; replaces the bare-question validator.
acceptance_criteria: A turn may contain a brief acknowledgement or reflection, an optional bridge or cited evidence, and one question; the single question-only validator is replaced by the ADR-013 speech-safety check.
Speech safety rejects any number, name, date or factual assertion not present in the participant's own words or a cited eligible excerpt.
The session has an opening that introduces the assistant and purpose, a stated recording and correction position, a time check and a closing.
Humour stays optional and light, is never aimed at a person's competence, accent or memory, and is absent when presenting a disagreement.
The example exchanges published in the interview-experience page can be reproduced by the running service.

items.title: SME S116 — Listen actively and confirm at the recap
items.scope: Backchannels, reflection and the confirmation model per ADR-016.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse optional backchannels signal attention and are never recorded as agreement.
The interviewer reflects the account back periodically in speech, and asks a spoken check only for high-impact ambiguity such as numbers, names and negation.
Per-turn transcript confirmation is removed from the voice path; contribution kind is inferred and corrected by the participant at the recap.
Every claim in the draft still traces to recap-confirmed wording and its transcript revision; unconfirmed material cannot enter a packet.
A correction at recap invalidates dependent derived notes exactly as a per-turn correction does today.

items.title: SME S117 — Interrupt respectfully and only when it earns it
items.scope: Interruption policy and participant controls; uses live evidence from SME-S121 when available.
acceptance_criteria: An unsolicited interruption requires a stable transcript, an identifiable question, and either a cited same-scope comparator or a critical capture problem.
A configurable cooldown and a single pending interruption prevent repeated challenge on one point; gentle, balanced and on-request settings are selectable during a session.
Non-urgent discrepancies are queued during a free account rather than interrupting it.
Interruption appropriateness is rated in trials and reported in aggregate, never as a judgement of the participant.

items.title: SME S118 — Choose the voice on conversational speech, not read passages
items.scope: Blinded conversational listening comparison with streamed first-chunk timing.
acceptance_criteria: Samples cover acknowledgement, reflection, a kind challenge and light humour, not only read passages.
At least one expressive British English challenger is compared with Voice B using streamed first-chunk timing rather than complete-file timing.
Content fidelity for numbers, dates and negation remains a mandatory gate regardless of the preference score.
The selection records sample size and individual variation and does not generalise from one listener.

items.title: SME S119 — Measure conversation quality against simulated participants
items.scope: Repeatable local harness and a Human rating sheet; repository automation only.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated participants hold a hidden ground-truth process with planted contradictions, unknowns, corrections and a genuine same-scope conflict.
A published rubric scores relevance, repetition, premise errors, listening behaviour and pace; development and holdout personas stay separate and the holdout is not tuned against.
Every iteration reports rubric scores and the SME-S114 turn-gap distribution alongside structural test results.
A one-page Human rating sheet captures naturalness, comfort, usefulness and fatigue.
No ADO Test Plans, Test Suites or Test Cases are created.

items.title: SME S120 — Derive the interview agenda from the Atlas ontology
items.scope: Read-only Atlas adapter and agenda construction; completes the evidence-pack intent of #1523.
acceptance_criteria: The agenda is built for a selected process from the Atlas ontology, Process Registry and Enterprise Activity Model: what is already held and can be verified, what is absent and must be elicited, and where existing sources disagree.
A second, materially different synthetic process runs end to end with no code change; fixture-specific wording and regular-expression guards are removed from the planner.
Evidence is pinned at session start with source version and hash; a changed or revoked pack blocks comparison rather than silently continuing.
Standalone operation without Atlas still works and states plainly that no evidence is available.
The adapter remains read-only: no Atlas source, section store or ontology write occurs.

items.title: SME S121 — Challenge and give back inside the live budget
items.scope: Live evidence lane within the 350 ms budget; no automatic conflict determination.
acceptance_criteria: The session evidence pack is prefetched and embedded at session start so a live comparison meets the 350 ms live-lane budget; budget expiry yields unchecked or needs-review, never verified.
Any spoken evidence statement quotes an eligible excerpt verbatim with its scope and version, and distinguishes what a source says from what is correct.
Live challenge precision at or above 95 per cent on labelled cases, with recall reported separately; a missing retrieval hit is never presented as absence of knowledge.
The interviewer can offer a relevant fact when asked or when it benefits the participant, always cited, and never fills a knowledge gap from model memory.
Deferred and background adjudication continue to own everything the live lane cannot settle.

items.title: SME S122 — Keep the session inside its time box
items.scope: Pacing, parking and hand-off to deferred validation.
acceptance_criteria: The agenda is paced against the agreed session length with a spoken time check; topics can be parked and the session extended only by agreement.
At the limit the session closes with uncovered topics listed explicitly rather than silently truncated.
Parked and unresolved points hand off to the deferred validation and follow-up work in #1532 and #1537.

items.title: SME S123 — Record the G1.5 conversation gate decision
items.scope: Human acceptance decision; no implementation work.
acceptance_criteria: A ten-minute unscripted headset conversation on a synthetic process runs with no button press between turns and no per-turn confirmation.
Human median rating at or above 4 of 5 for naturalness and pace, measured p50 at or below 1.5 s from end of speech to first substantive audio, and zero fabricated spoken facts.
The outcome, date and rationale are recorded in this Story and in the repository decision register.
A failed gate returns specific findings to SME-F13, SME-F14 or SME-F15; acceptance criteria are never lowered to pass it.

items.title: SME F17 — Tiberius sales workspace and product recall
items.gate: Internal sales rehearsal review; not customer or G1.5 acceptance
items.scope: User-authorised iterations 1 and 2 on 24 September: separate clean OpsAtlas Sales data and Tiberius product recall. Preserve existing corpus. Local-only voice; no wake-name or customer meeting delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Separate data, sessions, credentials and UI; existing workspace is not mutated.
Product records retain provenance and explicit internal review.
Spoken recall cites eligible evidence or reports unavailable knowledge.
User acceptance remains open; no automatic customer-claim approval.

items.title: SME S125 — Recall reviewed OpsAtlas product knowledge through Tiberius

items.scope: Eight pending curated records plus copied hashed originals. Local model chooses source IDs; exact eligible text is spoken via Chatterbox with visible evidence. Human enables records for internal rehearsal only.
acceptance_criteria: Distinguish available, experimental and unknown product claims; no invented pricing or ROI.
Unapproved, rejected, deleted or hash-changed evidence cannot answer a new question.
Revalidate selected evidence after inference and display citation information.
Demonstrate overview, offline/avatar distinction, pricing unknown and unsupported guarantee with real local speech.
Owner reviews the delivered corpus and accepts recall behaviour before story closure.
